mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises real discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for three consecutive months indicates labor market slack, which reduces wage growth and profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained unemployment above 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which depresses earnings and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO is persistently below its 12-month moving average for six months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% over two months signals a disinflationary tightening, which raises real rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises while CPIAUCSL < 2% for two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls below 2% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above their 12-month moving averages for three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA and RSAFS > 12-month MA for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and RSAFS are above their 12-month moving averages for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent fall in the unemployment rate below 4% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market that raises wage pressures and input costs, which compresses profit margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when the unemployment rate falls below 4% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals a recovery in residential construction activity, which boosts related equities and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month MA for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST is above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months.
